messages:
maria (ML Eng): Heads-up — trying to bring up archimedes-lite-8b quantized (4-bit) for private deployments. License text attached in the release tarball says: 'No wholesale redistribution of model weights without express permission; attribution required for derivative services.' Do we have a checklist for what we can ship to customers?

josh (Legal): Short answer: probably okay to serve, not okay to redistribute the raw quantized checkpoint. Need to see exact clause. If it says 'no wholesale redistribution' that's a block for shipping weights as-is. Serving via API or private instance is usually fine with attribution.

maria (ML Eng): Copy. The customer wants an on-prem package that includes the quantized weights + a small wrapper to run locally. That sounds like redistribution to me.

josh (Legal): Yeah that's redistribution. Two paths: 1) Ask upstream for a redistribution license (rare), or 2) deliver an installer that fetches weights at deploy time under end-user agreement where upstream terms are displayed — still risky. We should avoid handing binary weights.

sarah (Applied ML): From a product perspective, customers care about deterministic latency and small disk footprint; they asked for a tarball. Are there precedent deals where we negotiated a redistribution addendum?

josh (Legal): We've negotiated addenda for strategic partners before (see case `FENNEC-managed-custody`). It requires provenance, attribution, and royalties in some cases. For commercial redistribution, upstream often asks for attribution + a non-derivative/no-relicense clause.

legal-bot: License quick-check: found clause 'distribute' flagged in LICENSE.txt (line ~37). Recommendation: escalate to Legal Ops with the model repo URL + exact package we intend to ship.

liam (Infra): Operational note — if we can't ship weights, we can provide a sealed OCI image that pulls weights at runtime from a gated endpoint we control (customer pulls image, but weight fetch occurs under our gateway). That keeps custody but still lets the customer run locally in their VPC. Thoughts?

maria (ML Eng): That might work. Two implementation questions: 1) does that satisfy 'no redistribution' (custody stays with us), and 2) attribution — do we need to surface text in the UI/startup logs?

josh (Legal): 1) Seems better because we are not handing them the file directly. Need to document the data flow. 2) Attribution: yes — if license mandates attribution, include a NOTICE file and an opt-in acknowledgement screen or a header in the service that says 'Model: Archimedes-Lite-8b — original authors: <link>'. Be explicit in contract scope.

sarah (Applied ML): Also flag: embeddings. The license has a weird dataset-origin clause that may forbid commercial use of embeddings derived from certain training corpora. We should run our eval prompts through a filter and run a legal dataset-origin check before enabling embeddings for customers.

maria (ML Eng): Good catch. I'll add an eval job that runs a representative embedding batch and flags any prompt that mentions copyrighted corpus names (heuristic).

legal-bot: Action items created: #1 legal-review (attach model repo), #2 product-attribution-plan, #3 infra-gated-fetch-proposal.

josh (Legal): Next steps from Legal: send model LICENSE and checksum + planned delivery artifact (tarball vs OCI image) to legal-ops@redwood.ai. We'll triage and propose wording.

liam (Infra): If we go OCI-gated, I'll draft a minimal architecture doc. For auditability we should include an attestation log that records the fetch and the customer receipt.

maria (ML Eng): I'll pause the tarball build and switch to a proof-of-concept OCI image. Sarah — can you run the embedding legal check on the eval set by EOD?

sarah (Applied ML): On it. Will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

josh (Legal): Thanks team. If legal-ops flags anything blocking, we'll need product to push a change to the onboarding flow to collect the attribution acknowledgement before enabling the image.

maria (ML Eng): Got it. Will update once POC is up. :coffee:
